# raylib 5.5 bindings for Loi

Vendored Loi bindings for the [raylib](https://www.raylib.com/) 5.5 core API,
generated by [`tools/bindgen/bindgen.py`](../../tools/bindgen/bindgen.py).

## Provenance

- raylib **5.5** public `raylib.h` (the header reports `RAYLIB_VERSION "5.5"`).
- Generated on 2026-11-10 with the repository's binding generator and
  clang 21.1.8.
- Only the core `raylib.h` API is bound. `raymath.h`, `rlgl.h`, `raygui.h` and
  the audio streaming helpers are not part of this vendor directory.

Files:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `raylib.loi` | Generated Loi declarations: `opaque` handles, `shape`s, constants and `extern flow`s. |
| `raylib_shim.c` | Generated C shim for calls whose layout cannot cross the FFI boundary directly. |
| `skipped.txt` | Report of every declaration the generator deliberately did not bind, with a reason. |
| `include/raylib.h` | Vendored raylib 5.5 header used to generate and compile the shim. |

Generation summary: **410 flows**, **312 constants**, **17 shapes**,
**3 opaque handles** and **212 skipped declarations**.

## Building a program

```sh
loi build game.loi -o game \
    --c-source vendor/raylib/raylib_shim.c \
    --cc-flag -Ivendor/raylib/include \
    --cc-flag -lraylib \
    --cc-flag -lm
```

`--cc-flag` values are forwarded to the C compiler. On link steps they follow
the objects, so `-lraylib` resolves normally. `-lm` is needed by raylib's math
code on most Unix platforms. A system raylib installation works too: point
`--cc-flag -I...` at its include directory and link with `-lraylib`.

The generated shim includes the vendored header with a path relative to the
shim file, so the build does not depend on the repository root being the
working directory.

There is no raylib runtime in the development container, so these bindings and
the shim are syntax-verified (`loi check` and `clang -fsyntax-only`) but not
link- or run-tested here. A real window example needs a machine with raylib and
its platform dependencies (GLFW/OpenGL, X11 or Wayland, audio, ...) installed.

## What is skipped

The generator is conservative. The most common skips in this header are:

- records passed or returned by value whose C layout is not considered
  FFI-safe (`Camera3D` in some helpers, `Mesh`, `Model`, `Shader`, `Font`,
  `AudioStream`, `VrStereoConfig`, ...);
- callbacks (`AudioCallback`, `TraceLogCallback`) and variadic functions;
- raw pointers, pointer-to-pointer parameters and pointers to unsafe records;
- mutable `char *` buffers and empty macros.

Hand-write a small shim for the specific calls a program needs, expose it as
`extern flow ... as <symbol>`, and compile it with `--c-source`. `skipped.txt`
lists every skipped declaration and the reason.

## Regenerating

```sh
python3 tools/bindgen/bindgen.py \
    --header vendor/raylib/include/raylib.h \
    --include vendor/raylib/include \
    --output vendor/raylib/raylib.loi \
    --shim vendor/raylib/raylib_shim.c \
    --skipped vendor/raylib/skipped.txt \
    --module raylib
```

The generator requires `clang` with JSON AST support and Python 3.10+.
Regeneration is deterministic; commit the generated files together with the
header so builds do not depend on a local clang.
